Institutional Base Salary (IBS)

From the ORA eTraining module "Show Your Work: Understanding Time and Effort Reporting" (lesson 4 of 8).
What is Institutional Base Salary (IBS)?
Institutional Base Salary (IBS) is the total annual compensation paid by the institution for an individual's appointment, whether that time is spent on research, teaching, administrative duties, or other institutional activities.
IBS represents 100% of an individual's institutional effort.
It is the basis for calculating salary charges to sponsored projects.
It is not based on hours worked, but on total institutional responsibilities.

Institutional Base Salary: Composition
Base institutional salary
External consulting income
Compensation for research
Bonus pay (unless contractually part of base salary)
One-time payments not tied to institutional responsibilities

Compensation for administrative duties

Institutional Base Salary: Contract Restrictions
Faculty Contracts & IBS
For 9.5-month faculty, IBS consists of: (1) their 9.5-month academic year salary , and (2) up to 2.5 months of summer salary . This means faculty may receive additional compensation on sponsored projects during the summer months, but only within defined limits. Key Restrictions Total effort across all activities cannot exceed 100% IBS. Summer salary is limited to 26.3% of the faculty's academic-year salary. Faculty cannot "stack" multiple summer appointments beyond the 2.5-month limit.
Staff Contracts & IBS
For 12-month faculty and staff, IBS is defined as their full 12-month institutional salary , which already represents 100% effort . Key Restrictions Individuals cannot exceed 100% IBS Secondary contracts for additional pay on sponsored projects are not allowable Instead of additional compensation, release time or effort reallocation is possible. Administrative/clerical salaries cannot be charged directly when: (1) the work is routine (e.g., general admin support), (2) the role supports multiple projects or departments broadly, or (3) it is not specifically justified and approved in writing. Key Exceptions: Uniform Guidance Under 2CFR200.413(c) , the university is reimbursed for the cost of administrative and clerical salaries through the recovery of indirect costs on sponsored awards. However, they may be charged directly to a federal award only if specific conditions are met. The work must be essential to carrying out the project's programmatic objectives. For example, managing a complex training program with many participants. The role must be explicitly included in the proposal budget and justified to the sponsor. The sponsor must approve the cost either at the time of award or through prior written approval. The same cost cannot be charged both directly and through indirect cost recovery.

Knowledge Check
Knowledge check: A 12-month staff employee is asked to support a new NSF award for two months. What is the appropriate way to account for this effort?
  - Issue a secondary contract for the additional work  [incorrect]
  - Pay through employee via a stipend request  [incorrect]
  - Reallocate an equal portion of the employee's regular effort to the NSF award  [CORRECT ANSWER]
  - Charge the employee's time without adjusting their regular workload  [incorrect]
  If correct: Great job!
  If incorrect: Try again.
